dld.terminology.LA|Laos: Not established from the sources consulted. No Lao term for a childhood language disorder was found, and no category that a child with DLD would fall into. The UNESCO PEER profile for Lao PDR reports that "A definition of special education needs has not been found", and the operational definition it does record — from the 2011-15 National Strategy and Plan of Action on Inclusive Education — is built from social groups (girls and women, ethnic children, learners with disabilities, remote populations), not from types of impairment. A peer-reviewed 2020 account of cleft-palate speech services states there is no speech-language pathologist profession in the country, which is consistent with no clinical vocabulary having been settled. Searched: the UNESCO PEER Lao PDR inclusion profile, the 2020 IJPORL paper and its PubMed record, and general web search for speech and language therapy terminology and services in Lao PDR. No Lao Ministry of Education or Ministry of Health page naming such a category was located.

dld.identificationCriteria.AF|Afghanistan: Not established from the sources consulted. UNICEF's 2021 South Asia mapping records that there was no systematic screening or identification process in place for children with disabilities, and that identification was often limited to children already in school with physical or visible impairments, leaving out-of-school children with disabilities unidentified. The mapping describes the system as it stood before August 2021.
dld.identificationCriteria.AO|Angola: Not established from the sources consulted. UNICEF's 2023 regional mapping of disability-inclusive education lists no screening or identification tool for Angola, rates it as only initiating a disability identification system, and states that most countries in the region have no comprehensive or standardized system for identifying children with disabilities.
dld.identificationCriteria.CA|Canada: Not established from the sources consulted. Section 93 of the Constitution Act 1867 gives each provincial legislature the exclusive power to make laws in relation to education, so there is no federal body that identifies a language disorder and no national criteria to record. What exists is thirteen separate provincial and territorial answers.
dld.identificationCriteria.CD|DR Congo: Not established from the sources consulted. A Kinshasa logopede interviewed in 2017 describes the specialist multidisciplinary team that would follow such a child, and then states that this kind of procedure is not applied on a large scale in the country, so that parents are obliged to go first to a paediatrician. No Congolese instrument setting criteria for identifying a language disorder was reachable from this entry's sources.
dld.identificationCriteria.ER|Eritrea: Not established from the sources consulted. UNESCO's PEER profile records that Eritrea's 2010 National Education Policy does not contain specific guidelines on disability, and that developing an education support needs assessment was still listed as a strategy of the 2008 Policy and Strategy on Inclusive Education. UNICEF's 2023 regional mapping lists no screening or identification tool for Eritrea.
dld.identificationCriteria.GN|Guinea: Not established from the sources consulted. UNESCO's PEER profile records that Guinea does not seem to have adopted a conclusive definition of inclusive education in official documents at present, and that the term children with special educational needs refers simply to students with disabilities.
dld.identificationCriteria.IL|Israel: Not established from the sources consulted for this entry — the diagnostic criteria and any score thresholds applied by the statutory placement committees could not be determined from the English-language sources consulted. If you work in this system, this is exactly the field to fill in.
dld.identificationCriteria.LR|Liberia: Not established from the sources consulted. UNESCO's PEER profile records that no education policy on children and young people with disabilities has been adopted in Liberia, and that developing an inclusive education policy and guidelines is still only identified as a component of a student well-being programme.
dld.identificationCriteria.NG|Nigeria: Not established from the sources consulted. UNESCO's PEER profile records that a process for tracking early identification and referral for persons with special needs is not in place, and that the 2015 National Policy on Special Needs Education acknowledged the need to provide information to the public about diagnostic centres and referral mechanisms.
dld.identificationCriteria.SR|Suriname: Not established from the sources consulted. PEER records that there is no evidence of an inclusive education law in Suriname and therefore no official definition adopted in the country, so there is no instrument in which criteria could sit. It also records that the country has very limited capacity for early detection of disabilities.
dld.identificationCriteria.TD|Chad: Not established from the sources consulted. UNESCO's PEER profile records that no legislation or policy provides a fixed definition of inclusive education or of special educational needs in Chad, and that there is no formal supervision of inclusive education in the education system aside from a few isolated and fragmented initiatives.
dld.identificationCriteria.TM|Turkmenistan: Not established from the sources consulted. The UNESCO PEER profile states that an explicit definition of special education needs has not been found. It records medico-pedagogical commissions identifying children with speech disorders and referring them to specialized institutions, but states no evidence requirement, no threshold and no exclusion that those commissions apply.
dld.identificationCriteria.VA|Vatican City: Not established from the sources consulted. The Holy See's second periodic report to the Committee on the Rights of the Child records that children of Vatican City State attend legally recognised schools under various State legislation, and describes no school system inside the territory, so no body there identifies a language disorder.
dld.identificationCriteria.ZA|South Africa: Not established from the sources consulted for this entry — no national diagnostic or eligibility criteria were identified. The dominant constraint reported in the literature is not the criteria but the assessment tools available to apply them — see below. If you work in this system, this is exactly the field to fill in.

dld.referralPathway.MM|Myanmar: Not established from the sources consulted. The UNESCO PEER profile for Myanmar records that individual education plans and referral systems based on learning assessment are not in place, and that limited knowledge of needs assessment has been reported for teachers in regular schools and other personnel. The only service description found is a private Yangon hospital's own department page, which sets out no route by which a child reaches it and no gate on who may come. Searched: the PEER Myanmar inclusion profile and the Parami General Hospital speech and language therapy page.
